title: Make Japanese input work out of the box (JIS defaults + omarchy setup japanese)
head: 03b18a5e4e86
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Non-consuming Ctrl+Space is forwarded to the IME before an asynchronously spawned fcitx5-remote is guaranteed to deactivate it
leads.consequence: The JIS keybinding calls hl.exec_cmd, which forks a shell to invoke fcitx5-remote -c, and immediately returns as a non-consuming binding. Hyprland then forwards the same key event to the still-attached input method without waiting for the shell or fcitx's D-Bus acknowledgement. When Japanese input is active, the first prefix can still be handled by Mozc rather than the terminal, despite the manual's claim that direct input happens before the prefix goes through. This is an ordering race, not a claim that every press fails. Use a mechanism that waits for confirmed deactivation before forwarding/replaying the prefix, and test event delivery rather than only logging the command.
leads.triage: behavioural; sent neutral follow-up to Opus; confirmed from source that press normally reaches fcitx5 before -c and Mozc consumes Ctrl+Space during composition; published as optional doc note

leads.summary: Setup edits a different fcitx5 configuration tree when XDG_CONFIG_HOME or FCITX_CONFIG_HOME is customized
leads.consequence: With XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$HOME/custom, fcitx5 reads $HOME/custom/fcitx5/profile and config while setup writes $HOME/.config/fcitx5/*. The command stops and restarts the service, reports Mozc ready and JIS hotkeys freed, but Mozc and those hotkeys do not load; reruns repeat the wrong write. FCITX_CONFIG_HOME is an independent fcitx override: even if the setup uses XDG_CONFIG_HOME, the JIS callback also needs to resolve that fcitx-specific root. Set the configuration root once using fcitx's precedence and have both setup and JIS binding inspect that root.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus minor note 5 (pre-existing XDG_CONFIG_HOME); non-default config; dropped

leads.summary: Whitespace-valid fcitx5 hotkey sections survive replacement and fool the JIS trigger guard
leads.consequence: Given a valid user config section `[Hotkey/TriggerKeys] ` with 0=Zenkaku_Hankaku and 1=Control+space, fcitx's INI reader trims the section, but the AWK edit does not remove it. Setup appends a second canonical section with only 0=Zenkaku_Hankaku: fcitx merges them, retaining old 1=Control+space, while the Lua guard ignores the whitespace section and concludes the trigger has moved. In terminals Ctrl+Space still triggers fcitx and the callback also runs `fcitx5-remote -c`; the promised terminal-prefix behavior fails and the old toggle is silently retained. Trim sections consistently, and parse the complete effective list rather than searching literal lines.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus minor note 6 (hand-edited whitespace); fcitx5 never writes it; dropped

leads.summary: Mozc is added to Groups/0 rather than fcitx5's currently selected group
leads.consequence: With two legitimate groups, GroupOrder `0=Second`, `1=First` and Groups/0=First, Groups/1=Second, setup appends Mozc only to Groups/0 (or returns early because Mozc exists in an inactive group). fcitx5 selects the first *name* in GroupOrder as the current group, not the numeric 0 section. On restart the active group still has no Mozc, but the command says Japanese input is ready; rerunning it cannot fix that. Select the active group, or explicitly select and add to every intended group, using the daemon's group information.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus minor note 2 (Groups/0 vs GroupOrder); rare; dropped

leads.summary: Valid fcitx5 profile with formatting around Groups/0 is needlessly replaced
leads.consequence: A valid profile with `[Groups/0] ` (space after bracket), Name and Default Layout, existing items and no Mozc is parsed by fcitx5, but `grep -qx '\[Groups/0\]'` fails and setup replaces the entire profile after a backup. Previously configured input methods and groups disappear from the active configuration on restart. The printed backup path helps recovery but does not preserve the user's input methods as promised. Normalize INI section syntax or use fcitx5's group API rather than literal section greps.
leads.triage: hand-edited whitespace section header; same class as H2; dropped

leads.summary: Valid alternative Ctrl+Space key spelling bypasses the JIS guard
leads.consequence: fcitx5 accepts `CTRL_space` as a Ctrl+Space trigger, but the Lua guard looks only for exact `Control+space`. With a manually configured trigger 0=CTRL_space, the guard incorrectly decides fcitx5 no longer toggles, issues `fcitx5-remote -c` on the terminal prefix and undoes the user's Ctrl+Space toggle. Match fcitx's parsed key semantics, not a single serialized spelling, and add a test with the alternative accepted spelling.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus minor note 6 (CTRL_space); fcitx5 never writes it; dropped

leads.summary: Open keyboard-persistence PR #11418 adds a conflicting keyboard.lua and moves a test's target
leads.consequence: #11418 and #13327 both introduce default/hypr/keyboard.lua from an absent path with incompatible exports: #11418 returns `{layout,variant,options}`, whereas #13327 calls keyboard.vconsole() and keyboard.jis(). An automatic merge of that file produces conflict markers (local read-only merge-file exit 2); choosing either side unchanged breaks either #11418's input.lua/SDDM consumer or #13327's input.lua/JIS binding. #11418 also moves its non-Latin-list test to keyboard.lua, while this PR leaves that list in input.lua, so even a naive combination of tests fails. Integrate a single shared module/export and update both consumers and list test before merging both; GitHub marks #11418 MERGEABLE against quattro independently, not relative to this PR.
leads.triage: factual; verified directly: #11418 open (head 5585559b), adds default/hypr/keyboard.lua returning {layout,variant,options}; Opus self-check also confirmed input.lua overlap; published in Related PRs

leads.summary: Concurrent input-method installers promise hotkeys this PR removes on JIS keyboards
leads.consequence: The open #11719 Korean setup appends Hangul to the current group then promises the Hangul or Ctrl+Space toggle; the open #12312 Chewing setup likewise promises Ctrl+Space. On a JIS machine running this Japanese setup, all three of fcitx5's default trigger keys (including Hangul and Ctrl+Space) are replaced by Zenkaku_Hankaku, with Henkan/Muhenkan as activate/deactivate. If either companion setup later merges and its engine is installed, its advertised switch key no longer works, even when its group append succeeds. #9634 separately adds a second Mozc installer/menu command promising Ctrl+Space, creating duplicate Japanese flows and the same wrong hotkey claim after JIS setup. Coordinate a shared hotkey policy, guard messages by effective config, and avoid duplicate Mozc menu actions.
leads.triage: factual; verified directly in #9634/#11719/#12312 diffs (Ctrl+Space messages; #11719 also names 한/영); published in Related PRs

leads.summary: Append test doesn't load a valid fcitx5 profile or reject a broken group
leads.consequence: The `existing` fixture has `[Groups/0] Name=Mine` but no Default Layout, which fcitx5 rejects on load; grep-only assertions still call it a preserved Mozc profile. The append fixture uses only contiguous items in Groups/0 and greps for new text, not for a loadable current group. A plausible mutation that appends under the wrong group or leaves an invalid profile passes those assertions while the daemon silently falls back to its default group. Add a valid multi-group fixture with GroupOrder pointing to a different active group and assert fcitx5 loads/exports the expected group, at minimum validate required Default Layout and contiguous indices.
leads.triage: test fixture 'existing' lacks Default Layout; low value; dropped (Opus N1 covers the main test-fixture gap)

leads.summary: Counting item headings does not find the next readable fcitx5 ordinal
leads.consequence: Given a user-edited profile with valid group and items 0, 1 and 3, fcitx5 loads only indices 0 and 1 because its vector parser stops at the absent index 2. Setup counts three headings and writes Mozc into index 3 (a duplicate section), still leaving the hole at 2; Mozc never becomes part of a loaded group, yet setup prints success and subsequent reruns see Name=mozc and return early. Fill the first missing contiguous index or reconstruct the group from parsed entries, then verify the loaded list.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus minor note 3 (index gap); fcitx5 never writes gaps; dropped

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** At `03b18a5`, on JIS Mozc usually joins fcitx5's `keyboard-us` group; all points from the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13327#issuecomment-5853061410) are resolved, as the [reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13327#issuecomment-5853711017) says.

### On JIS, the vconsole layout usually no longer reaches the fcitx5 profile

fcitx5 saves its profile when `stop_fcitx5` stops it, usually the stock single `keyboard-us` group, and the new append path keeps it. A JIS install then gets `keyboard-us` + `mozc` with `Default Layout=us`, where `2d81b16` wrote `keyboard-jp`. **Impact** (fcitx5-mozc source, not run live): Mozc picks its kana table from the group layout, so kana input (かな入力) uses the US table; romaji should be unaffected.

**Suggested change:** when the group holds a single `keyboard-*` entry, write the vconsole-layout group as `2d81b16` did.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 03b18a5, passes at 2d81b16)</summary>

The `systemctl` stub models fcitx5 saving its stock profile on `stop`. Save as `test/shell.d/setup-japanese-stock-profile-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/setup-japanese-stock-profile-test.sh` from the repository root.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

# fcitx5 writes its in-memory profile when it exits (Instance's exit event calls
# save(), and SIGTERM from `systemctl --user stop` triggers it). On a session
# where fcitx5 is running, stop_fcitx5 therefore leaves fcitx5's own profile on
# disk before setup_input_method looks at it. Without customisation that is the
# stock single keyboard-us group fcitx5 builds when it cannot read an X11 layout.
# This stubs systemctl to do the same, then runs the command on a JIS layout.

set -euo pipefail

source "$(dirname "$0")/base-test.sh"

test_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$test_dir"' EXIT

stub_bin="$test_dir/bin"
mkdir -p "$stub_bin"

cat >"$stub_bin/systemctl" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
profile="$HOME/.config/fcitx5/profile"
if [[ $* == "--user stop omarchy-fcitx5.service" && ! -f $profile ]]; then
  mkdir -p "${profile%/*}"
  cat >"$profile" <<'EOF'
[Groups/0]
# Group Name
Name=Default
# Layout
Default Layout=us
# Default Input Method
DefaultIM=keyboard-us

[Groups/0/Items/0]
# Name
Name=keyboard-us
# Layout
Layout=

[GroupOrder]
0=Default
EOF
fi
STUB
# The same JIS layout for heads that read it from localectl instead.
cat >"$stub_bin/localectl" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
echo "   System Locale: LANG=en_US.UTF-8"
echo "      X11 Layout: jp"
STUB
for cmd in omarchy-pkg-add pkill sudo gsettings; do
  printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$stub_bin/$cmd"
done
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 1\n' >"$stub_bin/gum"
chmod +x "$stub_bin"/*

home="$test_dir/home"
mkdir -p "$home"
printf 'KEYMAP=jp106\nXKBLAYOUT=jp\n' >"$test_dir/vconsole.conf"

HOME="$home" PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" OMARCHY_VCONSOLE_PATH="$test_dir/vconsole.conf" \
  bash "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-setup-japanese" >"$test_dir/out" 2>&1 ||
  fail "setup japanese runs" "$(<"$test_dir/out")"

profile=$(<"$home/.config/fcitx5/profile")
printf -- '--- command output ---\n%s\n--- resulting profile ---\n%s\n---\n' "$(<"$test_dir/out")" "$profile"

grep -Fx 'Default Layout=jp' <<<"$profile" >/dev/null &&
  grep -Fx 'Name=keyboard-jp' <<<"$profile" >/dev/null &&
  grep -Fx 'Name=mozc' <<<"$profile" >/dev/null ||
  fail "a JIS keyboard gets Mozc after keyboard-jp when fcitx5 saved its stock profile on stop"
pass "a JIS keyboard gets Mozc after keyboard-jp when fcitx5 saved its stock profile on stop"
```

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Mechanism (fcitx5 5.1.23 source):** SIGTERM from `systemctl --user stop` makes fcitx5 exit, and its exit handler calls `save()`, which writes `profile` (`instance.cpp`, `inputmethodmanager.cpp`). Without X11 rule names, fcitx5's default group uses `us` (`buildDefaultGroup`). fcitx5-mozc derives its JIS flag from the group layout (`mozc_engine.cc`) and picks `kKanaJpMap` or `kKanaUsMap` from it (`fcitx_key_translator.cc`). The PR's JIS test starts without a profile, which the real flow does not normally produce after `stop`, so it passes. A user whose fcitx5 group layout is already `jp` is not affected.

**Verified** (sandbox runs and source):
- A missing `vconsole.conf` or one with only `KEYMAP` gives `keyboard-us`, and `jp,us` keeps only `jp`.
- A profile with other input methods keeps them and gains Mozc; a group-less profile is replaced and the backup path is printed.
- The prefix bind skips `fcitx5-remote -c` without a config, with fcitx5's default trigger keys (written out, or commented out as fcitx5 5.1.22+ saves them) and while `Control+space` is listed. It runs `-c` once the command has written its own trigger keys.
- The four PR test files pass, and all five mutants from the earlier review now fail.
- `default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc` merges cleanly with the current `quattro`.

**Optional notes:**
- **Documentation:** the manual says `Ctrl + Space` "switches to direct input before the prefix goes through". From Hyprland and fcitx5 source (not timed), the press normally reaches fcitx5 before `fcitx5-remote -c`; nothing orders the two. With nothing being composed, Mozc passes it on and the next key is likely direct. While composing, Mozc takes `Ctrl + Space` itself, so the prefix is lost and the pending text is committed. A note to confirm composition first would match.
- **Test:** a mutant that starts fcitx5 before writing the JIS hotkey lists still passes. fcitx5 reads its config at start, so the new keys would only apply after fcitx5 restarts or reloads its config. Having the `systemctl` stub also record the `config` at start would catch it.

**Related open PRs:**
- #11418 also adds `default/hypr/keyboard.lua`, returning `{ layout, variant, options }` instead of `vconsole()` and `jis()`, and rewrites `default/hypr/input.lua`, so whichever lands second conflicts.
- #12920 seeds the stock `keyboard-us` profile from `XKBLAYOUT`, but leaves a profile with more than one item alone. It would not repair a `keyboard-us` + `mozc` group made by this command.
- #9634, #11719 and #12312 tell users to press Ctrl+Space to switch (#11719 also names the 한/영 key); after this command on JIS neither key toggles.
</details>
